correctness.rationale: On this perfect-detection Markov life cycle with constant immigration, the local one-year bank is Y from the previous census, so successive visible pairs are the states. With u=1−d and w=u(1−c), independence gives q_yz=u−w(1−g0)^y(1−g1)^z. In coordinates (q00,a,b,r) this is (u−w,wg0,wg1,wg0g1), yielding w=ab/r. Positivity of q00, the strict inequalities on r and the upper bound on q00+w are exactly what is needed for 0<w<u<1 and 0<g0,g1<1. Substitution recovers every table entry. The determinant in the listed order is −u w² g0 g1, agreeing with the frozen formula; at g1=0 the lag contrast and determinant vanish. Every pair is reached with positive probability in two steps and the chain has self-loops, so stationary conditional denominators are positive. In the pair law, stationarity imposes pi01=pi10, and flow into 00 and 11 fixes pi01/pi00=q00/(1−q01) and pi11/pi01=q10/(1−q11). Conversely those two ratios and normalization give every pair frequency. Fixing the ratios gives two independent affine constraints in the open table domain, so each interior parameter has a local two-dimensional fiber even though the triple gives all four conditionals. The stationary linear solve and 256 exact rational round trips were independently replayed, including the frozen witness and a distinct witness with the same pair law.
residual_risks: This is structural identifiability for probability laws, not an estimate from three individual measurements. No generalization to heterogeneous, connectivity-dependent, imperfect-detection or longer-dormancy models.

value.rationale: For the constant-immigration ecological model used in real survey methodology, the exact short-horizon distinction matters: the pair law leaves continuous parameter ambiguity, whereas replicated three-census histories can in principle recover the full interior model. The feasible-table inequalities are a concrete diagnostic of compatibility with the assumed life cycle. The result isolates structural limitations and does not assert reliable estimation or that three realized observations suffice.
